so a different future vulnerability in the same package still fails the gate.

The gate prints every accepted finding on each run, and warns when an entry no
longer matches anything (dependency updated past it) so the list cannot silently rot.

GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2.title: React Router: RSC Mode CSRF Bypass Allows Action Execution Before 400 Response
GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2.why: Only reachable in React Server Components mode. BamDude is a plain SPA: App.tsx mounts <BrowserRouter>, and there is no @react-router/rsc, unstable_RSC, createCallServer or routeRSCServerRequest anywhere in frontend/src. The RSC request pipeline this bypasses does not exist in our bundle.
GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2.no_patch_on_our_line: Vulnerable range is >=7.12.0 <8.3.0 — there is no fix within 7.x. `npm audit fix --force` proposes downgrading to react-router-dom@7.11.0, which is a regression, not a fix.
GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2.resolution: Drops out on its own when the roadmapped React Router 8 upgrade lands (also needs react >=19.2.7; we are on 19.2.4). No separate action needed here — the gate will tell us this entry is stale.
